assumptions: Cases are author proposals against synthetic Search Console shapes. A live run needs a project-owned analytics.gsc connection with a selected property and a named payer; none is included here.

One Search Console property per saved workflow. Two equal-length windows of 14-90 days, ending at least three days before today so late-arriving data is excluded. Position is compared impression-weighted, never as an average of averages.
Every provider response is bounded by row_limit and a 64000-byte cap, so a response can be censored. A censored response bounds coverage; it never establishes that a page or query is absent.
Run success establishes that an artifact was delivered. A useful report additionally requires that each reported page carries exactly one verdict and the figures that selected it.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session at the existing pinned model pricing and spending ceiling. No managed-model routes are declared. The configured ceiling is not an expected price.
At most eight analytics.gsc calls including sites.list, each response capped at 64000 bytes, 900 seconds of runtime and one 192000-byte report.
Agent work scales with the number of pages considered, the size of the query mix and how much earlier-report continuity exists, not with the site's traffic.
Search Console is free and quota-limited by Google; it is not metered by Tin. Measured model cost requires verified usage from an authorized run, which this file does not contain.
effects: Read-only sites.list and search_analytics.read through the project's existing analytics.gsc connection. The property is chosen on the connection, never by the run.
One run-owned reports/content-refresh/<run_id>.md in project state, delivered through ordinary Files, Activity and immutable run history.
No page fetches, no content edits, no redirects, no Search Console changes, no email or publication, no workflow activation. Consolidation and retargeting are recommendations a human acts on.

cases.description: Two published pages each hold a quarter or more of the impressions on four shared queries, and both lost clicks. The self-competition rule outranks the decay rule, so the pair is consolidated rather than rewritten.

inputs.page_notes: Both guides were published in 2024 and cover overlapping ground.

cases.description: A page lost more than a third of its clicks while impression-weighted position held within 1.5 points. The report must send the operator to the result page rather than ask for a rewrite.
The page response returns exactly its row limit, so coverage is partial. Status must be partial, affected pages must fall to insufficient evidence, and no page may be called absent.
A page first observed inside the maturation window is reported as too young to judge, with the date it becomes judgeable, rather than as decayed.

inputs.page_notes: The pricing comparison went live six weeks ago.

cases.description: A fall the operator already explained in seasonality_notes is attributed to that cause and moved to leave alone, instead of generating work.

inputs.seasonality_notes: December is always quiet for us and the holiday campaign ended on the 20th.

cases.description: The connection exists but no Search Console property is selected. The run writes a diagnostic report naming the missing selection and makes no verdicts.

rubric.question: Does every reported page carry exactly one verdict, with the rule number that produced it and the figures that satisfied that rule?
Are positions combined impression-weighted rather than as an average of averages, and is that stated where positions are compared?
Does the report state, per reported page, how much of its impressions the query rows fail to account for, instead of treating the shortfall as an error?
Is every censored response named, with the verdicts that depend on it marked provisional, and is absence never inferred from a censored or failed request?
Is the section on what the report cannot tell you written for this run, naming actual merged URLs, remainders and composition shifts, rather than reusable boilerplate?
Does the report stop at retarget and decline to recommend deleting a page, on the stated grounds that it cannot see links, conversions or revenue?
